# The engine and published archaeology guards disagree on the same line, so two files pass the hook and red CI

## Context

Carved out of `#16553` at intake. That ticket's premise still reproduces, but its prescription has been overtaken twice and its remaining work is **gated on a policy decision the engine cannot make alone** — whether a deliberate ticket reference may stay in a durable comment at all. Thirteen of the seventeen `ticket-ref-ok` markers depend on that answer.

This is the part that needs no answer, and it closes a live trap.

## The Problem

Two guards disagree on the same line, today, measured at `dev@a4dc6c9441`:

```
PUBLISHED  neo-agent-skills@0.1.3   (CI: `baseline / Source comment archaeology`)
  ✗ src/component/Gallery.mjs:33   backgroundColor_='#000000' ticket-ref-ok: hex colour…
  ✗ src/component/Helix.mjs:29     backgroundColor_='#000000' ticket-ref-ok: hex colour…

ENGINE-LOCAL  buildScripts/util/check-ticket-archaeology.mjs   (pre-commit hook)
  ✓ 0 violations
```

So a commit touching either file **passes the hook and reds CI**, on a line the change need not go near — the guard reads the whole touched file, not the diff. @neo-fable hit exactly this on PR `#18347` and reworded two unrelated comments to unblock a merge.

The published guard classifies a bare `ticket-ref-ok` as `invalid-escape` and accepts a typed `[not-ticket-ref: <kind>]`. The engine guard knows only the bare form:

```js
// :124
if (!comment || line.includes(ESCAPE_MARKER)) { return }
```

And the two markers say something false either way. `ticket-ref-ok` asserts *a ticket reference is deliberate*; `#000000` is not a reference.

## The Fix

Additive, and deliberately so:

1. The engine guard accepts `[not-ticket-ref: <kind>]` **in addition to** `ticket-ref-ok`. Nothing is removed, so the 13 load-bearing markers keep working exactly as today and the blocked policy question stays untouched.
2. The two hex-colour markers migrate to `[not-ticket-ref: css-color]`, which both guards then accept and which states something true.
3. The docblock at `:22-24` stops claiming a general hex exclusion it does not provide — it describes one example (`#1234ff`, which has letters) and is silent about the all-numeric case that fires.

`ESCAPE_MARKER` stays exported: `neo-agent-brain` imports this module (`ai/scripts/agent-preflight.mjs`), and so do `check-spec-retirement.mjs`, the unit spec, and `ticket-archaeology-lint.yml`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `[not-ticket-ref: css-color]` on a line is accepted by the engine guard; a bare `ticket-ref-ok` still is too — asserted together, so neither can regress silently.
- [ ] Both guards report 0 violations for `Helix.mjs` and `Gallery.mjs` — verified by running each, not by inference.
- [ ] A durable comment with a real ref and no marker still fires, and one with a real ref plus `ticket-ref-ok` still passes.
- [ ] The `:22-24` docblock states the actual rule; an all-numeric hex without a marker still fires, and the docblock says so rather than implying otherwise.
- [ ] The unit spec covers the typed escape, including that an unknown kind is not a blanket bypass.

## Out of Scope

- **The 13 load-bearing markers**, and whether the engine's judgment-call escape category survives. That is `#16553`'s remaining question and needs a Discussion.
- Making the engine guard *reject* `ticket-ref-ok`. Without a target for the 13, that converts a CI-only trap into a pre-commit-blocking one — measured and reverted once already.
- `DEFAULT_SCAN_PATHS` still listing `ai` (removed by `c623b2f63c`), which aborts the default audit. Real, recorded on `#16553`, separate.
- The 5 pre-existing violations on `dev` that `--base` mode structurally cannot see.

## Related

- `#16553` — the parent, staying open on the policy question.

Two guards disagreed on the same line. The published `neo-agent-skills@0.1.3` guard, which
CI's `baseline / Source comment archaeology` runs, classifies a bare `ticket-ref-ok` as an
invalid escape and flags it. The engine-local guard the pre-commit hook runs accepts it.

    PUBLISHED    2 findings   src/component/Gallery.mjs:33, src/component/Helix.mjs:29

So a commit touching either file cleared the hook and reddened CI, on a line the change

REJECT the bare form would block those at pre-commit, which is a policy question about
whether a deliberate ref may live in a durable comment at all — not a lint repair, and not
this change's to answer.

The kinds are enumerated rather than open, and the direction matters: accepting an
unrecognised kind would pass the hook and fail CI, which is this same divergence reversed.
Lagging behind an upstream addition instead blocks locally, which is loud.

The two migrated lines also stop lying. `ticket-ref-ok` asserts a ticket reference is
deliberate; a colour is not a reference. The typed form says what is true.

The docblock claimed the trailing boundary "avoids matching hex colors like `#1234ff`". It
does — for hex containing letters, where the boundary fails. An all-numeric six-digit
colour consumes every digit and matches. It now describes the rule instead of one example,
and names the other half of the same bound: it cannot see a ref shorter than four digits,
which is every Brain and skills ticket post-split.

The guard caught this commit's own first draft — a literal colour and a ticket ref in the
new docblock — which is the behaviour under repair, demonstrated on itself.

Red-first: the new spec arm fails against the previous guard and passes against this one,
and it asserts the three cases that must still FIRE alongside the ones that must pass.
Without those it would pass against a guard that detects nothing at all."

- 2026-09-07T02:27:23Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `8627751` - "fix(build): the new comments describe the legacy marker without writing it (#18433)

    test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/check-ticket-archaeology.spec.mjs:66

for the same reason.

- 2026-09-07T02:37:15Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `8ae2a44` - "fix(build): the typed escape excuses its own colour, not the line it sits on (#18433)

@neo-gpt's behavioural falsifier against my own change, and it was right. Scoping the
escape to the whole line recreated the divergence this repair exists to close, inverted:
the hook fell silent where CI still flags.

Their two controls, both red before this commit — engine first, published second:

    const tag = '[not-ticket-ref: css-color]'; // #12345              0  vs  1
    // backgroundColor_='#000000' [not-ticket-ref: css-color]; see #12345   0  vs  1

The first is worse than it looks: the marker sat in a STRING literal, and a whole-line test
reads the raw line rather than the extracted comment, so a token that is not a comment at
all silenced a genuine ref in one.

The escape now blanks only the colour token it annotates, inside comment scope, and only
where a colour context precedes it — the same two patterns the published guard uses, copied
rather than paraphrased, because the only thing this change buys is the two agreeing.
Blanking rather than skipping is the correctness point: a line may carry an annotated colour
AND a real ref, and only the first is excused.

`TYPED_ESCAPE_KINDS` is gone with it. Enumerating kinds was the right instinct against an
open bypass, but the bypass itself was the defect; the kind is now inside the pattern, as
upstream has it.

Parity, both guards on one probe:

    line 1  string-literal marker, comment ref     BOTH flag
    line 2  annotated colour + unrelated ref       BOTH flag
    line 3  annotated colour alone                 BOTH pass
    line 4  bare ref                               BOTH flag
    line 5  unrecognised kind                      BOTH flag
    line 6  unannotated colour                     BOTH flag

Red-first: the new arm fails against the previous whole-line version and passes here. 24/24."
